newsitem.title: INDIA: SAIL April-May loss 2.79 bln rupees-paper.
newsitem.headline: SAIL April-May loss 2.79 bln rupees-paper.

text.p: Steel Authority of India Ltd (SAIL), India's largest steelmaker, has incurred a loss of 2.79 billion rupees ($77.9 million) in the first two months of 1997/98 (April-March), the Economic Times said on Monday.
The newspaper said SAIL, which in May announced a steep decline in its 1996/97 net profit, had been unable to raise prices by three percent and boost sales by 20 percent as earlier projected.
Sales in the first quarter of 1997/98 had grown by just seven percent, the Economic Times said. It quoted industry sources as saying the firm might end the year with a loss of seven billion rupees.
SAIL's 1996/97 net profit dropped to 5.27 billion rupees from 13.19 billion in the previous year.
The daily quoted SAIL chairman Arvind Pande as saying the company had not computed its profit or loss for the first two months of the 1997/98 financial year.
The firm plans to reduce its costs by 10 percent in 1997/98, improve the quality of its output and push exports to one million tonnes, Pande said.
